I am 71 years old, and I have farmed these 15.3 mu in Quzhou for 50 years. I only finished primary school, but I know my land better than any book. On about 10 mu I do wheat-maize rotation, and the other 5.3 mu I plant cotton.

For my winter wheat, I sow in October with an improved variety — not the most expensive seed, but the same kind my neighbor used last year and got 550 kg per mu. I till with the rotary tiller before sowing. For fertilizer, I spread one 50-jin bag of compound fertilizer per mu as base. Then at green-up time I spread 40 jin of urea per mu, and at jointing I add another 20 jin of urea. That comes to about 18 kg nitrogen per mu, and around 7 kg phosphorus and 6 kg potassium from the compound. I irrigate three times: wintering water, jointing water, and grain-filling water. I spray twice — once with herbicide at sowing, once for aphids if they come. I expect 550 kg per mu if spring is good.

My summer maize goes in right after wheat harvest in June. I use hybrid seeds — they cost more but they yield better, last year I got 620 kg per mu. I don't plough deep, just no-tillage sowing into the wheat stubble, because there is no time between harvest and sowing. I put 40 jin of compound fertilizer per mu at sowing, and at the big trumpet leaf stage I top-dress with 30 jin of urea per mu. That's about 16 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, 5 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate twice — once when it's young if it's dry, and once at tasseling. Two pesticide sprays, usually for corn borer.

Cotton is on 5.3 mu. I plant hybrid cotton in late April. I rotary till in spring. Cotton needs more potassium, so I put one bag of compound fertilizer plus an extra bag of potassium chloride per mu as base. Then I top-dress twice with urea, about 20 jin each time. That's about 14 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, 8 kg potassium per mu. Cotton needs more water and more medicine. I irrigate four times and spray four times for bollworm and aphids. I expect 260 kg of seed cotton per mu.

Fertilizer is expensive now, but I don't dare cut back. Two years ago I tried saving money on urea, the wheat turned yellow and I lost 50 kg per mu. Better to put a bit too much than too little. A bad harvest means I lose real money, wasting some fertilizer is just a cost. I watch what my neighbors do — if they all add more, I add more too. My son works in the city and sends some money home, but I still count every yuan. Change is risky, so I mostly do what I did last year.
